changeSet.author: ${claude}
changeSet.comment: Create system.notification_preferences, each user's choice of investment notifications (issue #540): the periodic report frequency, the month-end report, the frozen-holding alert and its minimum gain percentage. There is no backfill: a user without a row has the column defaults.
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE system.notification_preferences ( user_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES system.users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, periodic_report_frequency TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'DISABLED' CHECK (periodic_report_frequency IN ('DAILY', 'WEEKLY', 'BIWEEKLY', 'DISABLED')), month_end_report_enabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true, frozen_alert_enabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true, frozen_alert_minimum_gain_percentage NUMERIC(5, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.00 CHECK (frozen_alert_minimum_gain_percentage BETWEEN 0 AND 100), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL );

changeSet.author: ${claude}
changeSet.comment: Create system.notification_deliveries, the log of every report and alert sent (issue #540). The schedulers claim a (user, kind, period end) row before sending, and the unique constraint is what keeps a restart, a re-run or a second instance from sending the same email twice.
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE system.notification_deliveries ( id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, user_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES system.users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('DAILY_REPORT', 'WEEKLY_REPORT', 'BIWEEKLY_REPORT', 'MONTH_END_REPORT', 'FROZEN_ALERT')), period_end DATE NOT NULL, sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT notification_deliveries_user_kind_period_end_key UNIQUE (user_id, kind, period_end) );
